scenes.tts: The first film showed two populations drawing from one limited supply. If limits hold populations back, how can working together help? Gold food dots leave the tube and enter a honeybee colony. The same resource now moves along green paths. The picture changes, but the question about limited needs remains.
scenes.visual: Link directly from the first film. Carry over its COLOR MAP with one change: limited resource GOLD, the population being followed TEAL, cooperation GREEN, abiotic factor BLUE, and CORAL now means a living threat such as disease or predators. The shared tube fills most of the frame, then its gold food dots stream right as the glass transforms into a large honeycomb. Teal swimmers transform into teal worker-bee cartoons. Green paths begin growing between them.
scenes.narration: The first film showed two populations drawing from one limited supply. If limits hold populations back, how can working together help? Gold food dots leave the tube and enter a honeybee colony. The same resource now moves along green paths. The picture changes, but the question about limited needs remains.

scenes.visual: The moving green paths briefly frame the title: When Working Together Helps. Worker bees continue crossing the honeycomb.

scenes.tts: Cooperation happens when members of a population work together to meet their needs. In a colony, workers collect food, guard the hive, and care for young. They also pass liquid food from bee to bee. The shares are not always equal. The picture separates the jobs so their different effects stay easy to follow.
scenes.visual: Use one large honeycomb cross-section. Show on-screen text Tens of thousands can live here. One teal worker gathers a gold drop, one guards the entrance, and one tends a larva. Green paths connect their actions. A gold drop moves between two workers, then splits unequally into two visible portions.
scenes.narration: Cooperation happens when members of a population work together to meet their needs. In a colony, workers collect food, guard the hive, and care for young. They also pass liquid food from bee to bee. The shares are not always equal. The picture separates the jobs so their different effects stay easy to follow.

scenes.tts: Imagine every worker collecting food while nobody guards or cares for young. Which needs would go unmet? Watch the green paths, and decide what different jobs add to the group. Hold the whole colony in mind, not one worker.
scenes.visual: Reset the same hive. Transform every worker into a collector moving toward gold flowers. Leave the entrance and larva unattended. Fade in two large question marks over those places while green paths pulse without connecting.
scenes.narration: Imagine every worker collecting food while nobody guards or cares for young. Which needs would go unmet? Watch the green paths, and decide what different jobs add to the group. Hold the whole colony in mind, not one worker.

scenes.visual: Deliberate thinking pause. Keep the question visible. Collectors and gold drops continue moving slowly; the unguarded entrance and waiting larva remain clear.

scenes.tts: Different jobs connect several needs at once. One worker brings food, another guards, and another tends young. Together, the workers meet several colony needs at once. Each linked job supports needs that one collector cannot cover. Cooperation helps, but every worker still needs resources.
scenes.visual: Transform two collectors back into a guard and a caregiver. Green paths now connect flowers to food cells, the entrance, and the larva. Each path lights when its job succeeds. Keep the gold food store finite and gently falling as bees use it.
scenes.narration: Different jobs connect several needs at once. One worker brings food, another guards, and another tends young. Together, the workers meet several colony needs at once. Each linked job supports needs that one collector cannot cover. Cooperation helps, but every worker still needs resources.

scenes.tts: Other populations cooperate in different ways. A wolf pack can catch large prey such as elk. A tight school can make one fish harder for a predator to catch. Working together can help members get food or stay safe.
scenes.visual: Keep the honeycomb as a large frame. One green path transforms into a schematic wolf-pack arc around an elk silhouette. Another transforms into a tight moving school around a predator's missed strike. Label both examples schematic. Return both paths to the hive before the scene ends.
scenes.narration: Other populations cooperate in different ways. A wolf pack can catch large prey such as elk. A tight school can make one fish harder for a predator to catch. Working together can help members get food or stay safe.

scenes.tts: Cooperation does not remove limits. A limiting factor is anything in the environment that can restrict a population. Living factors are biotic, such as food, disease, and predators. Nonliving factors are abiotic, such as water and temperature. Shelter can be living or nonliving, depending on what provides it.
scenes.visual: Widen the hive world into a needs map. Gold food, a CORAL disease badge, and a CORAL predator silhouette enter a BIOTIC ring. BLUE water drops and a BLUE thermometer enter an ABIOTIC ring. Both rings press inward on a large teal population bar, which rises or falls while labels stay fixed.
scenes.narration: Cooperation does not remove limits. A limiting factor is anything in the environment that can restrict a population. Living factors are biotic, such as food, disease, and predators. Nonliving factors are abiotic, such as water and temperature. Shelter can be living or nonliving, depending on what provides it.

scenes.tts: Populations in a community are interdependent. A change in one can affect another. If disease reduces a rabbit population, foxes have less food. The disease strikes rabbits directly, then reaches foxes through their food link. The foxes can be affected even if the disease never infects them.
scenes.visual: Transform the needs map into a simple forest strip. A CORAL disease badge lowers a teal rabbit bar. A gold arrow labelled food runs from rabbits to a fox bar. As the rabbit bar falls, the arrow thins and the fox bar begins falling. Label the relationship schematic.
scenes.narration: Populations in a community are interdependent. A change in one can affect another. If disease reduces a rabbit population, foxes have less food. The disease strikes rabbits directly, then reaches foxes through their food link. The foxes can be affected even if the disease never infects them.

scenes.tts: Limited resources can restrict populations; cooperation can help members meet their needs. Both can happen in the same population. Cooperation changes what members can accomplish together. Help and limits belong in the same picture. It does not make food, water, shelter, disease, or predators disappear.
scenes.visual: Bring the hive and forest into two halves of one frame. Green cooperation paths brighten inside the teal population. Gold, coral, and blue limiting-factor symbols remain around it. Animate the population bar stabilizing below the top, showing help without unlimited growth.

scenes.visual: One-line end card only: 'Limited resources can restrict populations; cooperation can help members meet their needs.' No subtitle, title, logo, or second line. Green paths and gold food dots move very slowly behind the single line.
